PREVIOUS LESSON - Our Culture - Meaning of Cultural Diversity | Right Attitude towards Cultural Diversity in Our Society Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Civic Education

1. Lesson Introduction
2. Respect for People’s Views

4. How to Respect for People’s Views
5. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain why we must try to listen to other people’s views.
2. gives reasons why we must respect other people’s views, beliefs and traditions.
3. explain how to respect other people’s views, beliefs and traditions.
ENTRY BEHAVIOURS
The pupils know how to ask, listen and respect.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of real cultural materials and objects.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.

Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book - Basic Social Studies for Primary Schools 4 with Security Education by E E Ezewu, J A Olawepo, C C Anadi, J A Adeyanju.
All Relevant Materials
Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Being kind to people of other faiths is a must in a diverse world.
Just having that skill can help you develop a lot of great friendships and learn a lot about other traditions and cultures.
Everyone is entitled to his/her opinion. People’s views are the personal opinion, belief, attitudes about something or situation.
RESPECT FOR OTHER PEOPLE’S VIEWS
We must learn to listen to other people’s views, because:
1. there may be things to learn from them.
2. to show that we consider other people’s views important.
WHY WE MUST RESPECT OTHER PEOPLE’S VIEWS AND BELIEFS AND TRADITIONS
We must respect other people’s views so that -
1. there will be peace.
2. people will feel safe and happy.
3. you’ll learn new things and make better decisions.
4. you’ll make more interesting friends.
5. you’ll be a more progressive person.
6. you’ll make the world a better place.
LESSON 2 - HOW TO RESPECT FOR OTHER PEOPLE’S VIEWS, BELIEFS AND TRADITIONS
1. Look at people from other faiths as people, not as categories or religions.
2. Be informed about other faiths and customs.
3. Look for similarities.
4. Keep an open mind.
5. Remember that belief (including your own) is just that:belief.
6. Take care when talking about religion.
7. Avoid forcing your opinion or belief upon others.
WHAT DO WE GAIN BY RESPECTING OR LISTENING PEOPLE’S VIEWS
1. Harmony
2. Peace
3. Tolerance
4. Sharing
5. Trust
6. Safety
7. Love
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
1. Recites some traditional rhymes and songs to the pupils;
Pupil’s Activities - Recite some traditional rhymes and songs.
2. Helps pupils to appreciate why we should listen to other people’s views.
Pupil’s Activities - Discuss items 1-2 in content.
3. Invites a resource person to give a talk on why we should respect other people’s views  beliefs and traditions.
Pupil’s Activities - Listen to the resource person and ask questions.
4. Guides pupils to show how to have respect for other people’s views, beliefs and traditions.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in a demonstration on how to respect and tolerate other people’s views, beliefs and traditions.
5. Summary the key points on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Community Leadership - Meaning of Traditional Leadership | Duties of Traditional Leadership Primary 4 (Basic 4) - Civic Education
LESSON EVALUATION
Asks pupils to:
1. explain why we must to listen to other people’s views.
2. gives reasons why we must respect other people’s views, beliefs and traditions.
3. explain how to respect and tolerate other people’s views, beliefs and traditions.

2. given assistance to individual members of the Community.
3. promoting peace and unity.
4. encouraging community participation.

1. Togetherness
2. Love
3. Cooperation
4. Justice
5. Fair play
6. Sharing dialogue, etc.

topics.content:
GOVERNANCE: DEFINITION OF GOVERNANCE, MEANING OF GOOD GOVERNANCE AND DEMONSTRATING GOOD GOVERNANCE
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 1
THEME -  GOVERNANCE
PREVIOUS LESSON -
TOPIC - GOOD GOVERNANCE
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Governance
3. Meaning, Examples and Characteristics of Good Governance
4. Demonstrating Good Governance and Importance of Governance
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Define governance.
2. Explain the meaning of good governance.
3. Identify the characteristics of good governance.
4. State ways of demonstrating good governance.
5. Explain the importance of good governance in the school and community.
6. Demonstrate good governance through honesty, fairness, responsibility, and obedience to rules.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned about rules and regulations at home and in school, the importance of good behaviour, and respecting authority.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing the concept of governance and the qualities of good governance.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Charts showing good leadership and good governance
2. Pictures of community and school leaders
3. Flashcards with words such as honesty, fairness, responsibility, and participation
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every school has a head teacher, teachers, and class prefects who help to guide others and ensure that rules are followed. Communities and countries also have leaders who make decisions for the good of the people. When these leaders are honest, fair, responsible, and obey the law, they practise good governance.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the definition of governance, the meaning of good governance, and how they can demonstrate good governance in the classroom, at home, and in their community.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
Good governance is the fair, honest, transparent, responsible, and accountable way of managing the affairs of a community, school, organization, or country for the benefit of everyone.
Good governance promotes peace, justice, development, and respect for the rights of all people.
EXAMPLES OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
1. A class prefect who treats all pupils fairly.
2. A head teacher who listens to teachers and pupils before making decisions.
3. Community leaders who use public money honestly.
4. Citizens who obey laws and participate in community development.
CHARACTERISTICS OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
Good governance includes:
1. Honesty - Telling the truth and doing the right thing.
2. Fairness - Treating everyone equally without favouring anyone.
3. Accountability - Being ready to explain your actions and accept responsibility for them.
4. Transparency - Being open and not hiding important information.
5. Responsibility - Doing your duties well and taking care of what is entrusted to you.
6. Rule of Law - Obeying the laws and rules of the school or country.
7. Participation - Taking part in activities and helping to make good decisions.
8. Respect for the Rights of Others - Treating others kindly and respecting their opinions, property, and freedom.
LESSON 3 - DEMONSTRATING GOOD GOVERNANCE
We can demonstrate good governance by:
1. Obeying rules and regulations.
2. Being honest in our actions.
3. Treating everyone fairly.
4. Respecting the rights of others.
5. Participating in school and community activities.
6. Taking responsibility for our duties.
7. Protecting public property.
8. Reporting wrongdoing to the appropriate authority.
IMPORTANCE OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
Good governance helps to:
1. Promote peace and unity.
2. Encourage fairness and justice.
3. Protect people’s rights.
4. Improve development.
5. Build trust between leaders and followers.
6. Reduce corruption.
7. Promote responsible leadership.
8. Ensure that public resources are used wisely.
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Governance is best described as the process of _______.
A. making money through trade
B. leading and managing the affairs of a group
C. building roads only
D. organising sports competitions
2. Which of the following best describes good governance?
A. Allowing only friends to enjoy public resources
B. Governing with honesty, fairness, and responsibility
C. Ignoring the opinions of the people
D. Refusing to obey the law
3. Which action shows accountability?
A. Refusing to explain your actions
B. Blaming others for your mistakes
C. Accepting responsibility for your actions
D. Ignoring school rules
4. A class prefect who treats every pupil equally is showing _______.
A. pride
B. selfishness
C. anger
D. fairness
5. Which of the following is an example of participation?
A. Taking part in class discussions
B. Breaking school property
C. Refusing to work with others
D. Ignoring school activities
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences:. transparency, honesty, responsibility, participation, laws
6. Telling the truth shows _______.
7. Good leaders should be open and practise _______.
8. Doing your assigned work well shows _______.
9. Everyone should obey the _______ of the country.
10. Taking part in school activities is called _______.
C. True or False
11. Good governance promotes peace and unity. _______
12. Leaders should always be honest. _______
13. Good governance encourages corruption. _______
14. Everyone should obey the law. _______
15. Pupils can demonstrate good governance in school. _______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Honesty - A. Taking part in decision-making
17. Fairness - B. Telling the truth
18. Responsibility - C. Doing your duties well
19. Rule of law - D. Treating everyone equally
20. Participation - E. Obeying rules and laws
ANSWER KEYS
1. B. leading and managing the affairs of a group
2. B. Governing with honesty, fairness, and responsibility
3. C. Accepting responsibility for your actions
4. D. fairness
5. A. Taking part in class discussions
6. honesty
7. transparency
8. responsibility
9. laws
10. participation
11. True
12. True
13. False
14. True
15. True
16. B. Telling the truth
17. D. Treating everyone equally
18. C. Doing your duties well
19. E. Obeying rules and laws
20. A. Taking part in decision-making
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that governance is the process of leading, directing, and managing the affairs of a group, school, community, or country.
They also learned that good governance means leading and managing people with honesty, fairness, responsibility, transparency, accountability, participation, respect for the rule of law, and respect for the rights of others.
Pupils identified the characteristics of good governance and discussed practical ways of demonstrating good governance, such as obeying rules, telling the truth, treating others fairly, participating in school activities, protecting public property, and carrying out assigned responsibilities faithfully.
Finally, pupils understood that good governance promotes peace, unity, justice, development, trust, and responsible leadership, making the school, community, and country better places for everyone.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction - The teacher asks pupils to mention the leaders in their school (head teacher, class teacher, class prefect) and community. The teacher discusses what these leaders do before introducing the topic Governance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify leaders in their school and community and describe some of their responsibilities.
Step 2: Definition of Governance - The teacher explains that governance is the process of leading, directing, and managing the affairs of a group, school, community, or country. Also, the teacher gives simple examples from the classroom and school.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain governance in their own words and mention examples of governance in school.
Step 3: Meaning of Good Governance - The teacher explains that good governance means leading people with honesty, fairness, responsibility, transparency, accountability, and respect for the law. Also, the teacher discusses the characteristics of good governance:
- Honesty
- Fairness
- Accountability
- Transparency
- Responsibility
- Rule of law
- Participation
- Respect for the rights of others
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and explain the characteristics of good governance.
Step 4: Demonstrating Good Governance - The teacher explains practical ways of demonstrating good governance by:
- Obeying school rules.
- Telling the truth.
- Treating everyone fairly.
- Carrying out assigned duties.
- Participating in school activities.
- Respecting the rights of others.
- Protecting school property.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss ways they can practise good governance at home and in school.
Step 5: Practical Activity - The teacher presents different situations and asks pupils to identify whether they show good governance or poor governance.
Examples include:
- Returning a lost item.
- Keeping the classroom clean.
- Sharing leadership responsibilities.
- Refusing to cheat during a test.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the correct actions and explain why they represent good governance.
Step 6: Group Activity - The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following tasks:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of governance.
- Group 2: List the characteristics of good governance.
- Group 3: Demonstrate good governance through a short role play.
- Group 4: State the importance of good governance in the school and community.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, role-play, and present their findings.
Step 7: Lesson Summary - The teacher reviews the definition of governance, the meaning of good governance, its characteristics, and ways of demonstrating good governance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation - The teacher asks oral and written questions and observes pupils’ participation during the role play and class discussion.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions and demonstrate good governance through their responses and behaviour.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Types of Governance: Democratic, Economic and Financial Governance, and Features of Good Governance | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 2 Civic Education
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Define governance.
2. Explain the meaning of good governance.
3. Mention at least five characteristics of good governance.
4. State at least five ways of demonstrating good governance.
5. Explain the importance of good governance in the school and community.
6. Demonstrate good governance through honesty, fairness, responsibility, participation, and obedience to rules.

topics.content:
TYPES OF GOVERNANCE: DEMOCRATIC, ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL AND FEATURES OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 2
THEME -  GOVERNANCE
PREVIOUS LESSON - Governance: Definition of Governance, Meaning of Good Governance and Demonstrating Good Governance | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 1 Civic Education
TOPIC - TYPES OF GOVERNANCE
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Types of Governance
3. Democratic and Economic and Financial Governance
4. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
5. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of governance.
2. Identify the types of governance discussed in the lesson.
3. Explain the meaning of democratic governance.
4. Explain the meaning of economic and financial governance.
5. Mention the features of good governance.
6. State the importance of good governance in the school, community, and country.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned the meaning of governance, the meaning of good governance, and ways of demonstrating good governance.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing the types of governance and the features of good governance.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Charts showing democratic elections and government activities
2. Pictures of leaders, ballot boxes, and voters
3. Flashcards showing features of good governance
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every country needs good leaders to make decisions and manage its affairs. In Nigeria, leaders are chosen through elections, and they are expected to use the country’s money and resources wisely for the benefit of everyone. This is called governance.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about democratic governance, economic and financial governance, and the features of good governance that help a country develop peacefully and fairly.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF GOVERNANCE
Governance is the way leaders direct, manage, and make decisions for a group, community, organisation, or country.
TYPES OF GOVERNANCE
1. Democratic Governance
Democratic governance is a system in which the people choose their leaders through free and fair elections.
Features of Democratic Governance
In democratic governance,
- People vote to choose their leaders.
- Everyone has equal rights
- Leaders obey the law.
- Citizens participate in decision-making.
- People’s opinions are respected.
2. Economic and Financial Governance
Economic and financial governance is the proper management and use of a country’s money, resources, and property for the benefit of everyone.
Examples of Economic and Financial Governance
- Spending public money wisely.
- Preventing corruption.
- Collecting taxes responsibly.
- Providing public services such as schools and hospitals.
- Managing national resources honestly.
LESSON 2 - FEATURES OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
Good governance is characterised by:
1. Honesty
2. Fairness
3. Accountability
4. Transparency
5. Responsibility
6. Rule of law
7. Participation
8. Respect for the rights of others
IMPORTANCE OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
Good governance helps to:
1. Promote peace and unity.
2. Ensure justice and fairness.
3. Protect people’s rights.
4. Encourage development.
5. Reduce corruption.
6. Build trust between leaders and citizens.
7. Improve the standard of living.
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Governance is the process of ________.
A. buying and selling goods
B. leading and managing the affairs of a group or country
C. playing games
D. building houses
2. In democratic governance, leaders are chosen through ________.
A. competition
B. examinations
C. elections
D. interviews
3. Economic and financial governance is mainly concerned with ________.
A. organising sporting activities
B. managing public money and resources wisely
C. building only schools
D. teaching in classrooms
4. Which of the following is a feature of good governance?
A. Accountability
B. Corruption
C. Favouritism
D. Dishonesty
5. Which action shows good economic and financial governance?
A. Ignoring community needs
B. Stealing government money
C. Wasting public resources
D. Using public money wisely
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: honesty, elections, resources, transparency, participation
6. Democratic leaders are chosen through _______.
7. Good governance requires _______ in dealing with people.
8. Being open in decision-making is called _______.
9. Economic governance involves managing public __________.
10. Citizens should take part in community activities through _______.
C. True or False
11. Democratic governance disallows people to choose their leaders. _______
12. Good governance encourages corruption. _______
13. Accountability is a feature of good governance. _______
14. Economic and financial governance involves managing public money wisely. _______
15. Leaders should respect the rights of citizens. _______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Democratic governance - A. Telling the truth
17. Economic and financial governance - B. Managing public money and resources
18. Honesty - C. Taking part in decision-making
19. Rule of law - D. Leaders chosen through elections
20. Participation - E. Obeying the laws of the country
ANSWER KEYS
1. B. leading and managing the affairs of a group or country
2. C. elections
3. B. managing public money and resources wisely
4. A. Accountability
5. D. Using public money wisely
6. elections
7. honesty
8. transparency
9. resources
10. participation
11. False
12. False
13. True
14. True
15. True
16. D. Leaders chosen through elections
17. B. Managing public money and resources
18. A. Telling the truth
19. E. Obeying the laws of the country
20. C. Taking part in decision-making
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that governance is the process of leading and managing the affairs of a group, community, or country.
They learned two types of governance:
- Democratic governance, where people choose their leaders through free and fair elections.
- Economic and financial governance, which involves the proper management and use of public money and resources for the benefit of everyone.
Pupils also learned the features of good governance, which include honesty, fairness, accountability, transparency, responsibility, participation, the rule of law, and respect for the rights of others.
Finally, pupils understood that good governance promotes peace, justice, unity, responsible leadership, proper use of public resources, and national development, making the school, community, and country better places to live.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils how leaders are chosen in their school (for example, class prefects) and who manages school property and money. The teacher links their responses to the topic Types of Governance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify school leaders and explain how they are chosen and what they do.
Step 2: Meaning of Governance
The teacher explains that governance is the process of leading, directing, and managing the affairs of a group, community, or country.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of governance in their own words.
Step 3: Democratic Governance
The teacher explains that democratic governance is a system in which people choose their leaders through free and fair elections.
Also, the teacher discusses the features of democratic governance, such as:
- People vote for leaders.
- Everyone has equal rights.
- Leaders obey the law.
- Citizens participate in decision-making.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify examples of democratic governance in school and the community.
Step 4: Economic and Financial Governance
The teacher explains that economic and financial governance involves the proper management and use of public money and resources.
Examples include:
- Spending public money wisely.
- Providing schools and hospitals.
- Preventing corruption.
- Managing public resources responsibly.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways public money and resources should be used wisely.
Step 5: Features of Good Governance
The teacher discusses the features of good governance:
- Honesty
- Fairness
- Accountability
- Transparency
- Responsibility
- Rule of law
- Participation
- Respect for the rights of others
The teacher explains each feature with simple examples.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain each feature and give practical examples.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups and assigns the following tasks:
- Group 1: Explain democratic governance.
- Group 2: Explain economic and financial governance.
- Group 3: List the features of good governance.
- Group 4: State the importance of good governance in the school and community.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, identify, and present their findings.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of governance, the types of governance, and the features of good governance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher asks oral and written questions to assess pupils’ understanding of the lesson.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the evaluation questions, identify the types of governance, and explain the features of good governance.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

2. Identify the types of governance discussed in the lesson.

topics.content:
CIVIC EDUCATION

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Many pupils have seen or heard about government leaders such as the President, Governor, and Local Government Chairman. These leaders work at different levels to manage the affairs of the country, state, and local government. Government is divided into different levels so that responsibilities can be shared and services can reach the people.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of governance structure, the three levels of government in Nigeria, examples of leaders and institutions at each level, and how the government structure is arranged in a simple chart.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE
A governance structure is the way different levels, offices, and institutions of government are arranged to lead and manage a country.
In Nigeria, government is organised into three levels:
- Federal Government
- State Government
- Local Government
1. Federal Government
The Federal Government is the government that manages affairs that concern the whole country.
Examples of federal leaders and institutions include:
- The President
- The National Assembly
- Federal ministries and agencies
- The Supreme Court
2. State Government
The State Government manages the affairs of a particular state.
Examples include:
- The Governor
- State House of Assembly
- State ministries
- State courts
3. Local Government
The Local Government manages affairs at the local community level.
Examples include:
- The Local Government Chairman
- Councillors
- Local government departments
- Local services and facilities

IMPORTANCE OF GOVERNMENT STRUCTURE
A clear government structure helps to:
1. Divide responsibilities among different levels of government.
2. Bring government closer to the people.
3. Make decision-making easier.
4. Provide public services.
5. Promote law and order.
6. Encourage development in communities and states.
SIMPLE EXAMPLE
The Federal Government may handle matters affecting the whole country, the State Government manages matters within a state, while the Local Government handles  many issues affecting people at the local level.

SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that governance structure is the way different levels, offices, and institutions of government are arranged to manage the affairs of a country.
They learned that Nigeria has three levels of government:
- Federal Government - manages affairs that concern the whole country and is headed by the President.
- State Government - manages the affairs of a particular state and is headed by the Governor.
- Local Government - manages affairs at the local community level and is headed by the Local Government Chairman.
Pupils also learned about institutions such as the National Assembly, State House of Assembly, and Local Government Council. They understood that dividing government into different levels helps to share responsibilities, bring government closer to the people, provide public services, and promote development.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays a simple chart showing the Federal, State, and Local Governments and asks pupils to identify any government leaders they know.
The teacher explains that government is organised into different levels so that leaders can manage the affairs of the country, states, and local communities effectively.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify leaders such as the President, Governor, and Local Government Chairman.
Step 2: Meaning of Governance Structure
The teacher explains that a governance structure is the way different levels, offices, and institutions of government are arranged to manage the affairs of a country.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain governance structure in their own words.
Step 3: Federal Government
The teacher explains that the Federal Government manages matters that concern the whole country.
Examples include:

- National Assembly
- Federal ministries
- Federal agencies
- Federal courts
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the President as the head of the Federal Government and mention examples of federal institutions.
Step 4: State Government
The teacher explains that the State Government manages the affairs of a particular state.
Examples include:
- Governor
- State House of Assembly
- State ministries
- State agencies
- State courts
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the Governor as the head of the State Government and mention examples of state institutions.
Step 5: Local Government
The teacher explains that the Local Government manages affairs at the local community level.
Examples include:
- Local Government Chairman
- Councillors
- Local government departments
- Local services and facilities
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the Local Government Chairman and Councillors and discuss some services provided in their local government area.
Step 6: Government Structure Chart

Pupils’ Activities: Pupils copy and label the chart in their notebooks.
Step 7: Importance of Government Structure
The teacher explains that a clear government structure:
- Shares responsibilities among different levels.
- Brings government closer to the people.
- Makes decision-making easier.
- Helps provide public services.
- Promotes development.
- Helps maintain law and order.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention examples of how different levels of government serve people.
Step 8: Group Activity
The teacher divides the pupils into three groups:
- Group 1: Explain the Federal Government and give two examples of its institutions.
- Group 2: Explain the State Government and give two examples of its institutions.
- Group 3: Explain the Local Government and give two examples of its institutions.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their findings.
Step 9: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of governance structure, the three levels of government, their leaders, examples of institutions, and their importance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and explain the three levels of government.
Step 10: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise to assess their understanding of the lesson.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the exercise and identify the correct levels, leaders, and institutions of government.

CIVIC EDUCATION

THEME - GOVERNANCE

LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of good governance.
2. Describe transparency as a characteristic of good governance.
3. Explain the meaning of freedom of speech.
4. Explain the meaning of sincerity.
5. State why the provision of jobs is an important characteristic of good governance.
6. Mention the benefits of good governance to citizens.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the meaning of governance, types of governance, and the structure of government.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils the characteristics of good governance and why they are important in society.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of honest leaders serving the people
2. Charts showing the characteristics of good governance
3. Flashcards with key words (Transparency, Freedom of Speech, Sincerity, Jobs)

METHOD OF TEACHING

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Pupils have seen leaders in their school and community making decisions, giving instructions, and helping people. They have also seen people expressing their opinions, leaders telling the truth, and adults working in different jobs. Good leaders are expected to be honest, listen to the people, and create opportunities for citizens to work and live better lives.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the characteristics of good governance, including transparency, freedom of speech, sincerity, and the provision of jobs.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
Good governance is the proper and honest way of leading and managing the affairs of a country or community for the benefit of everyone.
CHARACTERISTICS OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
1. Transparency - Transparency means being open and honest in government activities. Leaders tell the truth and do not hide important information from the people.
2. Freedom of Speech - Freedom of speech means people have the right to express their opinions respectfully without fear, as long as they obey the law and respect others.
3. Sincerity - Sincerity means being honest, truthful, and faithful in carrying out duties. Good leaders keep their promises and work for the good of the people.
4. Provision of Jobs - A good government creates employment opportunities so that people can work, earn a living, and support their families.
LESSON 2 - IMPORTANCE OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
Good governance helps to:
1. Promote peace and unity.
2. Build trust between leaders and citizens.
3. Reduce corruption.
4. Improve the standard of living.
4. Create employment opportunities.
5. Encourage development.
6. Protect the rights of citizens.
WAYS CITIZENS CAN SUPPORT GOOD GOVERNANCE
Citizens should:
1. Obey the law.
2. Pay taxes.
3. Vote during elections.
4. Respect government property.
5. Report corruption.
6. Be honest and responsible.
7. Participate in community development.

SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that good governance is the honest, fair, and responsible way of leading and managing the affairs of a country or community for the benefit of everyone.
They learned four important characteristics of good governance:
- Transparency - being open and honest.
- Freedom of speech - allowing people to express their opinions respectfully.
- Sincerity - being truthful and faithful in carrying out duties.
- Provision of jobs - creating employment opportunities for citizens.
Pupils also learned that good governance promotes peace, unity, trust, development, employment, and a better standard of living. Citizens should support good governance by obeying the law, being honest, paying taxes, voting during elections, and protecting public property.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of leaders addressing citizens, people working in different jobs, and a community meeting.
The teacher asks:
- Who are the people in the pictures?
- What are the leaders doing?
- What makes a good leader?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Good Governance
The teacher explains that good governance is the honest, fair, and responsible way of leading and managing the affairs of a country or community for the benefit of everyone.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of good governance in their own words.
Step 3: Characteristics of Good Governance
The teacher explains the following characteristics:
Transparency
- Leaders are open and honest.
- They do not hide important information from the people.
Freedom of Speech
- Citizens can express their opinions respectfully.
- People should speak responsibly without breaking the law.
Sincerity
- Leaders should be truthful and faithful.
- They should keep their promises.
Provision of Jobs
- Good governments create employment opportunities.
- Jobs help people earn a living and support their families.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss examples of transparency, sincerity, freedom of speech, and job creation.
Step 4: Importance of Good Governance
The teacher explains that good governance:
- Promotes peace.
- Encourages unity.
- Builds trust.
- Reduces corruption.
- Improves the standard of living.
- Creates employment.
- Promotes national development.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the benefits of good governance.
Step 5: How Citizens Can Support Good Governance
The teacher explains that citizens should:
- Obey the law.
- Be honest.
- Pay taxes.
- Vote during elections.
- Protect public property.
- Report corruption.
- Participate in community development.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss how they can support good governance at home, in school, and in their community.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups.
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of transparency and give two examples.
- Group 2: Explain freedom of speech and state why it is important.
- Group 3: Explain sincerity and describe how a sincere leader behaves.
- Group 4: Explain why the provision of jobs is important and mention four benefits of good governance.
Each group presents its answers to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their work.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of good governance, its characteristics, and the importance of good governance.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise to assess their understanding.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the multiple choice, fill-in-the-gaps, true or false, and matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

GOVERNMENT: MEANING AND TYPES OF GOVERNMENT
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 5
THEME - GOVERNMENT
PREVIOUS LESSON - Characteristics of Good Governance: Transparency, Freedom of Speech, Sincerity and Provision of Jobs | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 4 Civic Education

LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of government.
2. Mention the three main types of government.
3. Describe the features of democratic government.
4. Describe the features of traditional government.
5. Describe the features of military government.
6. State the importance of government in society.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about governance, the types of governance, and the characteristics of good governance.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing the meaning of government and the different types of government.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:

METHOD OF TEACHING

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Pupils have seen government officials, traditional rulers, soldiers, and people voting during elections. They have also seen government provide schools, hospitals, roads, and security in their communities. These activities show that government is responsible for leading the people and providing important services.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of government, the different types of government, and how each type helps to lead and serve the people.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF GOVERNMENT
Government is the group of people who make laws, lead a country, state, or community, and provide services for the people.
Government works to maintain peace, protect lives and property, and promote the welfare of citizens.
TYPES OF GOVERNMENT
1. Democratic Government
2. Military Government
3. Traditional Government
LESSON 2 - DEMOCRATIC GOVERNMENT
A democratic government is a government in which the people choose their leaders through free and fair elections.
Features of Democratic Government
- People vote during elections.
- Citizens enjoy freedom of speech.
- Leaders are elected for a specific period.
- The rule of law is respected.
TRADITIONAL GOVERNMENT
A traditional government is a system of leadership headed by traditional rulers such as kings, chiefs, emirs, obas, or obis.
Features of Traditional Government
- Leadership is usually based on tradition or inheritance.
- Traditional rulers help to settle disputes.
- They promote peace and preserve culture.
- They advise government on community matters.
MILITARY GOVERNMENT
A military government is a government controlled by the armed forces after taking over power, usually without an election.
Features of Military Government
- Leaders are soldiers.
- People do not elect the leaders.
- Military rule is usually temporary.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF GOVERNMENT
Government helps to:
1. Make and enforce laws.
2. Maintain peace and order.
3. Protect lives and property.
4. Provide schools and hospitals.
5. Build roads and bridges.
6. Create employment opportunities.
7. Promote national development.

SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that government is the group of people who lead a country, state, or community, make laws, and provide services for the people. They learned the three main types of government taught at this level:
- Democratic Government - leaders are elected by the people through free and fair elections.
- Traditional Government - led by traditional rulers such as kings, chiefs, emirs, obas, or obis.
- Military Government - controlled by the armed forces, usually after taking over power without an election.
Pupils also learned that government is important because it makes laws, maintains peace and order, protects lives and property, provides schools and hospitals, builds roads, creates jobs, and promotes national development.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of a President/Governor, people voting during an election, a traditional ruler (Oba, Emir, Obi, or Chief), and soldiers.
The teacher asks:
- Who are the people in these pictures?
- What do they do?
- Who leads our country?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Government
The teacher explains that government is the group of people who lead a country, state, or community, make laws, and provide services for the people.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of government in their own words.
Step 3: Types of Government
The teacher explains the three main types of government.
Democratic Government
- Leaders are chosen through elections.
- Citizens vote for their leaders.
- People enjoy freedom of speech.
- Leaders serve for a specific period.
Traditional Government
- Led by kings, chiefs, emirs, obas, or obis.
- Leadership is based on tradition or inheritance.
- Traditional rulers help to maintain peace and preserve culture.
Military Government
- Controlled by the armed forces.
- Leaders are soldiers.
- People do not elect military leaders.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the characteristics of each type of government.
Step 4: Importance of Government
The teacher explains that government:
- Makes and enforces laws.
- Maintains peace and order.
- Protects lives and property.
- Provides schools and hospitals.
- Builds roads and bridges.
- Creates jobs.
- Promotes national development.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the importance of government in their community.
Step 5: Class Discussion
The teacher leads a discussion on the type of government practised in Nigeria. Also, the teacher explains that Nigeria practises democratic government, where leaders are elected through voting.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify Nigeria’s type of government and explain how leaders are chosen.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups.
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of government and mention its functions.

INTRODUCTION

They have also heard about the President, Governors, lawmakers, and judges performing different duties in the country. These people belong to different parts of the government and work together to ensure peace, justice, and development.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the three arms of government-the Legislative, Executive, and Judiciary-and the important roles each arm performs in governing the country.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF THE ARMS OF GOVERNMENT
The arms of government are the three main parts of government that work together to govern a country. Each arm has its own duties and responsibilities.
The three arms of government are:
- Legislative
- Executive
- Judiciary
LESSON 2 - ARMS OF GOVERNMENT
1. Legislative Arm
The Legislative arm is responsible for making laws for the country.
Members of the legislative arm are called lawmakers.
Examples include:
- Senate
- House of Representatives
- State House of Assembly
Functions of the Legislative Arm
- Makes laws.
- Amends laws.
- Represents the people.
- Checks the activities of the executive.
2. Executive Arm
The Executive arm is responsible for implementing and enforcing laws.
It is headed by the:
- President (Federal Government)
- Governor (State Government)
- Chairman (Local Government)
Functions of the Executive Arm
- Implements laws.
- Maintains peace and security.
- Provides public services.
- Develops the country.
3. Judiciary Arm
The Judiciary is responsible for interpreting laws and settling disputes.
Judges and magistrates work in the judiciary.
Functions of the Judiciary
- Interprets laws.
- Settles disputes.
- Protects the rights of citizens.
- Ensures justice is served.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF THE ARMS OF GOVERNMENT

CIVIC EDUCATION

THEME - GOVERNMENT

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of the functions of government.
2. Mention at least six major functions of government.
3. Explain how government protects lives and property.
4. State the importance of government in providing education and healthcare.
5. Identify some basic amenities provided by the government.
6. Explain why the functions of government are important to citizens.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the meaning of government, the types of government, and the three arms of government.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils the major functions of government and how these functions improve the lives of citizens.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS

INTRODUCTION
Pupils have seen government build schools, hospitals, roads, and markets in their communities. They have also seen police officers maintaining peace and security, teachers working in public schools, and doctors treating sick people in government hospitals. These are some of the important duties performed by the government for the benefit of the people.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the major functions of government and understand why these duties are important for the welfare and development of citizens.
MEANING OF THE FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT
The functions of government are the important duties and responsibilities carried out by the government to ensure the well-being, peace, and development of the country.
MAJOR FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT
1. Making and Enforcing Laws - Government makes laws and ensures that people obey them.
2. Protecting Lives and Property - Government protects people and their property through the police, military, and other security agencies.
3. Providing Education - Government builds schools and provides teachers and learning materials for pupils.
4. Providing Healthcare - Government builds hospitals and health centres to care for sick people.
5. Providing Good Roads and Transportation - Government builds and repairs roads and bridges to make travelling easier.
6. Creating Employment - Government creates jobs so that people can work and earn a living.
7. Providing Basic Amenities - Government provides important services such as:
- Clean water
- Electricity
- Public markets
- Good drainage
- Parks and recreational centres
8. Promoting Peace and National Development - Government works to maintain peace, unity, and the development of the country.
IMPORTANCE OF GOVERNMENT FUNCTIONS TO CITIZENS
The functions of government help citizens to:
1. Live peacefully.
2. Enjoy security.
3. Receive quality education.
4. Access healthcare services.
5. Travel on good roads.
6. Get employment opportunities.
7. Enjoy better living conditions.
9. Promote national development.

Pupils also learned that these functions help citizens to live safely, receive education and medical care, enjoy better living conditions, travel easily, get employment opportunities, and contribute to the development of the country.

- Why are these services important?

The teacher divides the class into four groups.

- Group 3: State the importance of security, roads, and job creation.
- Group 4: List five basic amenities provided by the government and explain why they are important.
Each group presents its answers to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their work.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the major functions of government and their importance to citizens.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the multiple choice, fill in the gaps, true or false, and matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Pupils have seen people voting during elections, traditional rulers leading their communities, and soldiers protecting the country. These leaders serve the people in different ways and belong to different systems of government. Although these systems have different methods of leadership, they all help to maintain peace, order, and development.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the similarities and differences between democratic, traditional, and military governments and understand how each type of government serves the people.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF TYPES OF GOVERNMENT
Types of government are the different ways a country or community is governed.
The three types learned are:
- Democratic Government
- Traditional Government
- Military Government
SIMILARITIES AMONG THE TYPES OF GOVERNMENT
Although they are different, they all:
1. Provide leadership.
2. Maintain peace and order.
3. Make decisions for the people.
4. Promote the welfare of citizens.
5. Help to develop the community or country.
LESSON 2 - DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE TYPES OF GOVERNMENT
1. Democratic Government
- Leaders are elected by the people.
- Citizens vote during elections.
- People enjoy freedom of speech.
- Leaders serve for a fixed period.
2. Traditional Government
- Led by kings, chiefs, emirs, obas, or obis.
- Leadership is based on tradition or inheritance.
- Traditional rulers preserve culture and customs.
- They help to settle disputes in their communities.
3. Military Government
- Led by soldiers.
- Leaders are not elected by the people.
- The military takes control of government.
- Military rule is usually temporary.
IMPORTANCE OF UNDERSTANDING THE DIFFERENT TYPES OF GOVERNMENT
Knowing the different types of government helps pupils to:
1. Understand how leaders are chosen.
2. Appreciate good leadership.
3. Respect traditional institutions.
4. Know the rights and responsibilities of citizens.
5. Become responsible future leaders.

In this lesson, pupils learned that there are three main types of government: democratic, traditional, and military government. They learned that these types of government are similar because they all provide leadership, maintain peace and order, and work for the development of the people.

PROBLEMS FACING GOVERNMENT: CHALLENGES OF THE FEDERAL, STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND THEIR SOLUTIONS
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 10
THEME - GOVERNMENT
PREVIOUS LESSON - Differences Between the Various Types of Government: Similarities and Differences | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 9 Civic Education
TOPIC - PROBLEMS FACING GOVERNMENT AND THEIR SOLUTIONS
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Problems Facing Government and Their Solutions
3. Importance of Solving Government Problems
4. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
5. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of problems facing government.
2. Mention at least six problems facing the Federal, State, and Local Governments.
3. Suggest ways of solving the problems facing government.
4. Explain the importance of solving government problems.
5. State how citizens can help government overcome these challenges.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the functions of government and how government provides services for the people.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils the problems that make it difficult for government to perform its functions and the possible solutions.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of bad roads, hospitals, schools, and security officers
2. Pictures showing corruption, unemployment, and flooding
3. Chart showing the problems facing government and their solutions
4. Flashcards
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Pupils have seen bad roads, flooding, unemployment, damaged public facilities, and news about insecurity in their communities or on television. They have also seen government repairing roads, building schools, creating jobs, and providing security to solve these problems. These challenges make it difficult for the government to provide all the services people need.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the problems facing the Federal, State, and Local Governments, their possible solutions, and how citizens can help government solve these challenges.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF PROBLEMS FACING GOVERNMENT
Problems facing government are the challenges that make it difficult for the government to provide good services and develop the country.
COMMON PROBLEMS FACING GOVERNMENT
1. Corruption - Some public officers misuse government money or property for personal gain.
2. Lack of Funds - Government may not have enough money to provide all the needed services.
3. Unemployment - Many people do not have jobs, making it difficult for families to meet their needs.
4. Insecurity - Crimes such as theft, kidnapping, and violence make it difficult for government to maintain peace.
5. Poor Roads and Infrastructure - Bad roads, damaged bridges, and poor public facilities affect transportation and development.
6. Poor Maintenance of Public Property - Some government facilities are damaged because people do not take good care of them.
7. Population Growth - A rapidly increasing population puts pressure on schools, hospitals, roads, and other public services.
8. Natural Disasters - Floods, erosion, and other natural disasters can damage roads, buildings, and farms.
LESSON 2 - SOLUTIONS TO GOVERNMENT PROBLEMS
Government can solve these problems by:
1. Fighting corruption.
2. Using public money wisely.
3. Creating more jobs.
4. Improving security.
5. Building and repairing roads and public facilities.
6. Providing quality education and healthcare.
7. Encouraging citizens to protect public property.
8. Working together with citizens to promote national development.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF SOLVING GOVERNMENT PROBLEMS
Solving these problems will:
1. Improve the standard of living.
2. Promote peace and security.
3. Reduce poverty.
4. Create employment opportunities.
5. Encourage national development.
6. Improve public services.
7. Make life better for everyone.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Problems facing government are called ______.
A. games
B. celebrations
C. challenges
D. rewards
2. Which of these is a problem facing government?
A. Honesty
B. Corruption
C. Unity
D. Kindness
3. Which problem occurs when many people do not have jobs?
A. Unemployment
B. Education
C. Farming
D. Transportation
4. Which of these helps to protect lives and property?
A. Shopping
B. Cooking
C. Singing
D. Security
5. Which of these can damage roads and buildings?
A. Painting
B. Reading
C. Dancing
D. Flooding
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: corruption, roads, jobs, funds, security
6. Government needs enough ______ to provide services.
7. Bad ______ make transportation difficult.
8. Government should create more ______ for citizens.
9. Fighting ______ helps government use money wisely.
10. Government should improve ______ to protect lives and property.
C. True or False
11. Corruption is a challenge facing government. ______
12. Good roads help national development. ______
13. Citizens should destroy public property. ______
14. Creating jobs helps to reduce unemployment. ______
15. Government and citizens should work together to solve problems. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Corruption - A. Lack of jobs
17. Unemployment - B. Damaged public facilities
18. Poor roads - C. Misuse of public money
19. Insecurity - D. Lack of peace and safety
20. Lack of funds - E. Not enough money
ANSWER KEYS
1. C. 2. B. 3. A. 4. D 5. D
6. funds
7. roads
8. jobs
9. corruption
10. security
11. True
12. True
13. False
14. True
15. True
16. C - Misuse of public money
17. A - Lack of jobs
18. B - Damaged public facilities
19. D - Lack of peace and safety
20. E - Not enough money
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that problems facing government are challenges that make it difficult for the government to provide services and develop the country. They identified common problems such as corruption, lack of funds, unemployment, insecurity, poor roads, poor maintenance of public property, population growth, and natural disasters.
Pupils also learned that these problems can be reduced by fighting corruption, creating jobs, improving security, using public funds wisely, building and repairing public facilities, and encouraging citizens to protect government property and cooperate with the government.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures of bad roads, flooding, unemployed youths, police officers, damaged public facilities, and road construction.
The teacher asks:
- What do you see in these pictures?
- Which of these are problems in our community?
- How can these problems affect the people?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Problems Facing Government
The teacher explains that problems facing government are challenges that make it difficult for the government to provide services and develop the country.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of problems facing government in their own words.
Step 3: Common Problems Facing Government
The teacher explains the common problems facing the Federal, State, and Local Governments.
- Corruption
- Lack of funds
- Unemployment
- Insecurity
- Poor roads
- Poor maintenance of public property
- Population growth
- Natural disasters
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify and discuss the problems.
Step 4: Solutions to Government Problems
The teacher explains that government can solve these problems by:
- Fighting corruption.
- Using public money wisely.
- Creating more jobs.
- Improving security.
- Building and repairing roads.
- Providing good education and healthcare.
- Maintaining public property.
- Working together with citizens.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils suggest other ways government can solve these problems.
Step 5: Importance of Solving Government Problems
The teacher explains that solving government problems helps to:
- Improve the standard of living.
- Promote peace and security.
- Reduce poverty.
- Create employment.
- Improve public services.
- Encourage national development.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain why it is important for government to solve these problems.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups.
- Group 1: List five problems facing government.
- Group 2: Explain five ways government can solve these problems.
- Group 3: State five ways citizens can help government solve these challenges.
- Group 4: Explain five benefits of solving government problems.
Each group presents its answers to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their work.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the problems facing government, their solutions, and the importance of solving them.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the multiple-choice, fill-in-the-gaps, true-or-false, and matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of problems facing government.
2. Mention at least six problems facing the Federal, State, and Local Governments.
3. Suggest five ways of solving the problems facing government.
5. Explain five importance of solving government problems.

SOLUTIONS TO THE PROBLEMS FACING GOVERNMENT: PROMOTING GOOD GOVERNMENT AND FIGHTING BRIBERY AND CORRUPTION
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 4 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 11
THEME - GOVERNMENT
PREVIOUS LESSON - Problems Facing Government: Challenges of the Federal, State and Local Governments and Their Solutions | Primary 4 (Basic 4) First Term Week 10 Civic Education
TOPIC - SOLUTIONS TO THE PROBLEMS FACING GOVERNMENT
LEARNING
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Good Governance and Ways of Promoting Good Governance
3. Meaning and Examples of Bribery and Corruption
4. Ways of Fighting Bribery and Corruption
5. Importance of Fighting Bribery and Corruption
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of solutions to government problems.
2. Explain the meaning of good governance.
3. Mention the ways of promoting good governance.
4. Explain the meanings of bribery and corruption.
5. State the ways of fighting bribery and corruption.
6. Explain the importance of promoting good governance and fighting bribery and corruption.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the problems facing the Federal, State, and Local Governments.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils the solutions to these problems, including promoting good governance and fighting bribery and corruption.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures showing honest leaders at work
2. Pictures illustrating bribery and corruption (appropriate for children)
3. Chart showing ways of promoting good governance
4. Flashcards
5. Newspapers or magazine pictures related to good governance
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Pupils have learned that government faces many challenges such as corruption, unemployment, poor roads, and insecurity. They have also seen people who are honest and hardworking, as well as people who misuse public money or demand bribes. Good leadership and honest behaviour help government solve these problems and improve the lives of citizens.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the solutions to government problems, the meaning of good governance, and how bribery and corruption can be prevented to make the country better for everyone.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF SOLUTIONS TO GOVERNMENT PROBLEMS
Solutions to government problems are the actions taken by the government and citizens to overcome challenges and improve the country.
MEANING OF GOOD GOVERNANCE
Good governance is the proper and honest way of leading a country or community for the benefit of everyone.
Ways of Promoting Good Governance
1. Being honest in leadership.
2. Using public money wisely.
3. Obeying the law.
4. Being transparent and accountable.
5. Providing quality education and healthcare.
6. Creating employment opportunities.
7. Listening to the needs of the people.
8. Ensuring justice and fairness.
9. Protecting lives and property.
10. Encouraging peace and unity.
LESSON 2 - MEANING OF BRIBERY
Bribery is giving or receiving money, gifts, or favours to get unfair advantages.
Examples of bribery:
- Giving money to avoid punishment.
- Offering gifts to receive special treatment.
MEANING OF CORRUPTION
Corruption is the dishonest use of power or public money for personal gain.
Examples of corruption:
- Stealing government money.
- Misusing public property.
- Awarding jobs unfairly.
Ways of Fighting Bribery and Corruption
1. Be honest at all times.
2. Refuse to give or receive bribes.
3. Report corrupt practices to the appropriate authorities.
4. Punish people who engage in corruption.
5. Use public money responsibly.
6. Teach children good moral values.
7. Obey the law.
8. Encourage transparency and accountability.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF FIGHTING BRIBERY AND CORRUPTION
Fighting bribery and corruption helps to:
1. Promote good governance.
2. Improve public services.
3. Protect government property.
4. Create fairness and justice.
5. Reduce poverty.
6. Encourage national development.
7. Build trust between the government and citizens.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. Good governance means ______.
A. honest and proper leadership
B. fighting in the community
C. wasting public money
D. breaking the law
2. Bribery means ______.
A. giving or receiving money for unfair favour
B. helping the poor
C. planting trees
D. obeying the law
3. Corruption is the ______.
A. dishonest use of public money or power
B. building of schools
C. teaching in class
D. cleaning the environment
4. Which of these promotes good governance?
A. Honesty2
B. Corruption
C. Theft
D. Violence
5. Which of these helps to fight corruption?
A. Reporting corrupt practices
B. Giving bribes
C. Destroying public property
D. Telling lies
B. Fill in the Gaps
Use the following words to complete the sentences: honesty, bribery, corruption, law, transparency
6. Good governance requires ______.
7. We should refuse ______.
8. ______ is the dishonest use of public money.
9. Good citizens obey the ______.
10. Good governance encourages ______.
C. True or False
11. Good governance promotes national development. ______
12. Bribery is a good habit. ______
13. Corruption affects the development of a country. ______
14. Citizens should support corrupt practices. ______
15. Honesty helps to fight corruption. ______
D. Match Column A with Column B.
Column A - Column B
16. Good Governance - A. Giving or receiving unfair favour
17. Bribery - B. Good moral value
18. Corruption - C. Openness in leadership
19. Honesty - D. Dishonest use of power
20. Transparency - E. Honest leadership
ANSWER KEYS
1. C 2. D 3. D 4. A 5. C
6. honesty
7. bribery
8. corruption
9. law
10. transparency
11. True
12. False
13. True
14. False
15. True
16. E. Honest leadership
17. A. Giving or receiving unfair favour
18. D. Dishonest use of power
19. B. Good moral value
20. C. Openness in leadership
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that government problems can be solved through good governance and by fighting bribery and corruption. They learned that good governance means leading with honesty, transparency, accountability, fairness, and respect for the law.
Pupils also learned that bribery is giving or receiving money or gifts for unfair favour, while corruption is the dishonest use of public money or power for personal gain. They identified ways to fight bribery and corruption, such as being honest, refusing bribes, obeying the law, reporting corrupt practices, and using public money wisely.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher displays pictures showing honest leaders, people refusing bribes, police officers arresting criminals, and citizens protecting public property.
The teacher asks:
- What do you see in these pictures?
- Which actions are good?
- Which actions are wrong?
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and answer the questions.
Step 2: Meaning of Solutions to Government Problems
The teacher explains that solutions to government problems are the actions taken by government and citizens to overcome challenges and improve the country.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning in their own words.
Step 3: Meaning of Good Governance
The teacher explains that good governance means leading honestly, fairly, and responsibly for the benefit of everyone.
The teacher discusses ways of promoting good governance:
- Being honest.
- Obeying the law.
- Using public money wisely.
- Being transparent.
- Providing good services.
- Protecting lives and property.
- Creating jobs.
- Promoting peace and unity.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways of promoting good governance.
Step 4: Meaning of Bribery and Corruption
The teacher explains:
- Bribery is giving or receiving money, gifts, or favours to get unfair treatment.
- Corruption is the dishonest use of public money or power for personal gain.
The teacher gives simple examples.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify examples of bribery and corruption.
Step 5: Ways of Fighting Bribery and Corruption
The teacher explains that bribery and corruption can be reduced by:
- Being honest.
- Refusing to give or receive bribes.
- Reporting corrupt practices.
- Obeying the law.
- Using public money wisely.
- Punishing offenders.
- Teaching good moral values.
- Encouraging transparency.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils suggest other ways to fight bribery and corruption.
Step 6: Group Activity
The teacher divides the class into four groups.
- Group 1: State five ways of promoting good governance.
- Group 2: Explain the meanings of bribery and corruption with examples.
- Group 3: List five ways of fighting bribery and corruption.
- Group 4: Explain five benefits of good governance to citizens.
Each group presents its work to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 7: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meanings of good governance, bribery, corruption, and the ways to solve government problems.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise the lesson.
Step 8: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils the practice exercise.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils complete the multiple choice, fill in the gap, true or false, and matching questions.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to,
1. Explain the meaning of solutions to government problems.
2. Explain the meaning of good governance.
3. Mention at least six ways of promoting good governance.
4. Explain the meanings of bribery and corruption.
5. State at least six ways of fighting bribery and corruption.
6. Explain the importance of promoting good governance and fighting bribery and corruption.
